h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ל״ח Pesach — Maamar Lamed Ches

p: וַיֵּט מֹשֶׁה אֶת יָדוֹ וְגוֹמֵר וַיּוֹלֶךְ ה' רוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה וְגוֹמֵר וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת הַיָּם לֶחָרָבָה
"And Moshe stretched out his hand, etc., and Hashem drove a strong east wind, etc., and made the sea dry land"
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, כ"א).
(Shemos 14:21).
לְהָבִין הָעִנְיָן: לָמָּה עָשָׂה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הָרוּחַ קָדִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ סִיבָּה לִבְקִיעַת הַמַּיִם, שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
We must understand: why did Hashem, may He be blessed, bring about the east wind as though a natural intermediary were needed for splitting the waters, as we find in the Gemara
(גִּיטִּין ל"א:):
(Gittin 31b):
רוּחַ קָדִים חֲרִישִׁית וְכוּלֵּי בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמְּנַשֶּׁבֶת עוֹשָׂה תְּלָמִים תְּלָמִים בַּיָּם?!
"The gentle east wind, etc., when it blows, makes furrows upon furrows in the sea"?
וַהֲלֹא בְּקִיעַת הַיָּם לֹא הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הָרוּחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
Surely the splitting of the sea did not occur through the wind, as it is said
(תְּהִלִּים קי"ד, ה'-ז'):
(Tehillim 114:5-7):
מַה לְּךָ הַיָּם כִּי תָנוּס וְגוֹמֵר מִלִּפְנֵי אָדוֹן חוּלִי אָרֶץ מִלִּפְנֵי אֱלוֹהַּ יַעֲקֹב,
"What ails you, O sea, that you flee, etc.? Tremble, O earth, before the Master, before the God of Yaakov,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
and as they said in the Midrash
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ו')
(Shemos Rabbah 21:6)
שֶׁהַיָּם לֹא רָצָה לְהִקָּרַע עַד שֶׁנָּתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יְמִינוֹ עַל יְמִינוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
that the sea refused to split until the Holy One, blessed is He, placed His right hand upon Moshe's right hand, as it is said
(יְשַׁעְיָה ס"ג, י"ב):
(Yeshayahu 63:12):
מוֹלִיךְ לִימִין מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹמֵר!
"Who led at the right hand of Moshe, etc."!
וְאִם כֵּן לָמָּה נִצְרָךְ הָרוּחַ קָדִים? כְּמוֹ רֶגַע הָיָה לְהַיָּם לְהִקָּרַע מִלִּפְנֵי אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב!
If so, why was the east wind necessary? In a single instant the sea would have split before the God of Yaakov!
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן הוּא: דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַגָּלֻיּוֹת הוּא לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית, שֶׁהוּא חֵטְא דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
However, the explanation is that the root purpose of all exiles is to rectify the blemish of the covenant, which was the sin of the Generation of the Flood, as it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית ו', י"ב):
(Bereishis 6:12):
כִּי הִשְׁחִית כָּל בָּשָׂר וְגוֹמֵר
"For all flesh had corrupted its way, etc."
וְנִשְׁטְפוּ בַּמַּיִם.
and they were swept away in water.
וְגָלוּת רִאשׁוֹן הָיָה בְּמִצְרַיִם שֶׁהִיא עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְבָּרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִדַּת צַדִּיק,
And the first exile was in Egypt, which is "the nakedness of the land," so that Israel would be refined in the attribute of Tzaddik [guardian of the covenant],
וְאִיתָא
and it is stated
(בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִיזַ"ל)
(in the writings of the Arizal)
דְּאוֹתָן הַנְּפָשׁוֹת בְּעַצְמָן שֶׁהָיוּ בַּמַּבּוּל הָיוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם, וְנִגְזַר עֲלֵיהֶם: הַיְאֹרָה תַּשְׁלִיכֻהוּ, רַק דְּמֹשֶׁה הִצִּילָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ

that those very same souls from the Generation of the Flood were reincarnated in Egypt, which is why "into the river you shall cast him" was decreed upon them, except that Moshe saved them, as they said
(סוֹטָה י"ב:)
(Sotah 12b)
עַל הַפָּסוּק
on the verse
(בְּמִדְבַּר י"א, כ"א):
(Bamidbar 11:21):
שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת אֶלֶף רַגְלִי הָעָם אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי בְּקִרְבּוֹ
"'Six hundred thousand footmen are the people in whose midst I am'"
בִּשְׁבִילִי נִצַּלְתֶּם כּוּלְּכֶם.
"[Moshe said:] Because of me you were all saved."
וְהַיָּם מוֹרֶה עַל הַתַּאֲווֹת שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ מַיִם הַזֵּדוֹנִים,
Now the sea symbolizes lusts, which are called "the treacherous waters,"
וּבֶאֱמֶת הָיָה עוֹד טְעָנוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעִנְיָן זֶה גַּם כֵּן:
and in truth there were still heavenly accusations against Israel regarding this matter as well:
וְאַף דְּאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
for even though it is stated in the Midrash
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד', כ"ה)
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:25)
שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶם פָּרוּץ בְּעֶרְוָה וְכוּלֵּי,
that not a single one of them was found to be licentious in immorality, etc.,
וְהַקִּטְרוּג עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
and the prosecution against Israel brought in Midrash Rabbah
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ז')
(Shemos Rabbah 21:7)
שֶׁהָיָה: הַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵּי,
was "These are idol worshippers, etc.,"
וְכֵן בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה
and likewise in Vayikra Rabbah
גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי — אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ עֲרֵלִים, אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מְגַדְּלֵי בְּלוֹרִיּוֹת וְכוּלֵּי, לוֹבְשֵׁי כִּלְאַיִם
"'A nation from the midst of a nation'—these were uncircumcised and those were uncircumcised, these grew pagan locks and those grew pagan locks, etc., wearers of kilayim"
מַשְׁמַע שֶׁבַּעֲרָיוֹת לֹא הָיָה קִטְרוּג עֲלֵיהֶם,
which might imply there was no prosecution against them regarding immorality
אַךְ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
nevertheless, in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ק"ע:)
מְפוֹרָשׁ קִטְרוּג רַהַב בְּגִילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים;
it is explicitly stated that Rahav [Egypt's guardian angel] prosecuted them regarding immorality, idolatry, and bloodshed;
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ אַף שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדוּרִים מִן הָעֶרְוָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה עֲלֵיהֶם טְעָנוֹת בִּשְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית.
so perforce, even though they fenced themselves off from actual illicit relations, there were still accusations against them regarding inner purity and guarding the covenant.
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' מ"ט.):
מַה חָמָא יַמָּא? אֲרוֹנָא דְּיוֹסֵף חָמָא וְעָרַק מִקַּמֵּיהּ, בְּגִין דִּכְתִיב
"What did the sea see? It saw the coffin of Yosef and fled before him, because it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית ל"ט, י"ב):
(Bereishis 39:12):
וַיָּנָס וַיֵּצֵא הַחוּצָה
'And he fled and went outside'
וְעַל דָּא: הַיָּם רָאָה וַיָּנֹס
and therefore 'The sea saw and fled'"
(וְכֵן הוּא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פ"ז, ח').
(and so it is in Bereishis Rabbah 87:8).
וְהָעִנְיָן הוּא דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים עַל שֵׁם יוֹסֵף: שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף
The meaning is that all Israel are called by the name of Yosef—"the remnant of Yosef"
שֶׁיּוֹסֵף מְבָרֵר כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל: וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים, כֵּיוָן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִיקְרֵי צַדִּיק;
because Yosef refines and elevates all Israel—"And your people are all righteous," for once circumcised, one is called Tzaddik;
שֶׁכֵּן כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הַשְּׁבָטִים, אַף שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה נִכְלָל קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ בְּכָל הַשְּׁבָטִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
for indeed the holiness of each of the twelve tribes, even though each had his own unique sanctity, was nevertheless included within all the tribes, as it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית מ"ט, כ"ח):
(Bereishis 49:28):
אִישׁ כְּבִרְכָתוֹ בֵּרַךְ אֹתָם
"Each according to his blessing he blessed them"
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה צ"ט, ד')
(Bereishis Rabbah 99:4)
וְזֶה: הַיָּם רָאָה וַיָּנֹס.
and this is "The sea saw and fled."
וְזֶה דְּאִיתָא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא
And this is what is stated in the Mechilta
(Beshalach 4):
לְגוֹזֵר יַם סוּף לִגְזָרִים — לִגְזִירִים
"'To Him Who divided (gazeir) the Sea of Reeds into parts'—read it as gezirin (the circumcised)"
דְּכֵיוָן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִיקְרֵי צַדִּיק.
for once a person is circumcised, he is called Tzaddik.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this is what is said
(תְּהִלִּים קי"ד, ד'):
(Tehillim 114:4):
הֶהָרִים רָקְדוּ כְאֵילִים, גְּבָעוֹת כִּבְנֵי צֹאן
"The mountains skipped like rams, the hills like young sheep"
יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לְצֹאן שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז גַּם כֵּן לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית, דִּכְתִיב
Israel are compared to sheep, which also alludes to the holiness of the covenant, as it is written
נֹהֵג כַּצֹּאן יוֹסֵף.
"Who leads Yosef like a flock."
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכִין לְכָל הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ, בְּנֵי הָאָבוֹת וְהָאִמָּהוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים, כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And Israel merit all levels of holiness by virtue of being holy seed, the children of the holy Patriarchs and Matriarchs, as stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' קי"ב: וְתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן כ"א)
(Vol. 2, 112b, and Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21)
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ
and in the Midrash
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ט"ו, ד'):
(Shemos Rabbah 15:4):
הָרִים אֵלּוּ אָבוֹת וּגְבָעוֹת אֵלּוּ אִמָּהוֹת.
"Mountains—these are the Patriarchs; and hills—these are the Matriarchs."
וְעִנְיַן הָרִיקּוּדִין שֶׁהוּא הֲרָמַת הָרַגְלַיִם שֶׁרוֹמְזִים עַל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ, הֲרָמָתָם הוּא הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַיְסוֹד,
And the matter of dancing—which is lifting the feet, symbolizing the unlearned masses—their elevation comes entirely through the holiness of Yesod,
וְזֶה שֶׁנּוֹהֲגִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לִרְקוֹד בְּשִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה לִרְמוֹז עַל זֶה: וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים.
and this is why Israel have the custom to dance during the joy of a mitzvah, to allude to this: "And your people are all righteous."
וְלַאֲשֶׁר שֶׁאָז בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף הָיָה עוֹד טְעָנוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעִנְיָן זֶה, לָזֶה נֶאֱמַר:
Now, because back then at the Splitting of the Sea there were still accusations against Israel in this regard, therefore it is written:
וַיּוֹלֶךְ ה' אֶת הַיָּם בְּרוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה כָּל הַלַּיְלָה וְגוֹמֵר
"And Hashem drove the sea back with a strong east wind all that night, etc."
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נָשַׁב בִּלְבָבוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל רוּחַ טָהֳרָה לְטַהֲרָם מִתַּאֲווֹת הַנִּקְרָאִים מַיִם הַזֵּדוֹנִים,
for through this, a spirit of purity blew within the hearts of Israel to cleanse them from the lusts called "the treacherous waters,"
וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת הַיָּם לֶחָרָבָה וַיִּבָּקְעוּ הַמָּיִם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ מִמֵּילָא "הַיָּם רָאָה וַיָּנֹס", שֶׁרָאָה אֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף.
"and He made the sea dry land, and the waters were split"—so that afterward, automatically, "the sea saw and fled," recognizing the coffin of Yosef [and Israel's inner covenantal purity].
וְכֵן נִרְאֶה מִזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם שֶׁכָּל הַלַּיְלָה הָיָה בְּדִינָא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עֲלַיְיהוּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: מַעֲשֵׂי יָדַי טוֹבְעִין בַּיָּם

And so it appears from the holy Zohar there, that all night long the Holy One, blessed is He, stood in strict judgment over Israel, regarding which He said, "My handiwork [Israel] are in danger of drowning in the sea"
וְהוֹעִיל הָרוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל לְטַהֵר לְבָבָם מִכָּל תַּאֲוָה, וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת הַיָּם לֶחָרָבָה.
and the strong east wind worked within the heart of Israel to purify their hearts from all lust, and thus "He made the sea dry land."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 6 — “The main rectification of this flaw was at the Splitting of the Sea. Even though there was prosecution against them, it was then clarified that all the evil in Israel comes through the kelipah and impurity of Egypt; the Egyptians took their portion in Gehinnom, and Israel took all the life and holy sparks that were in Egypt. And this is ‘the sea saw and fled’: it saw the coffin of Yosef, which clarifies that ‘your people are all righteous,’ and through this ‘it fled,’ and the Egyptians took the portion of evil that was in them and were drowned.” Connection: The same reading of the sea fleeing before Yosef’s coffin; it adds that the Egyptians drowned bearing the evil that had clung to Israel, while Israel took the sparks, the “spoils of the sea.”
